groups.title: Oral liquid (B38500ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as a tonic and for physical tiredness, and to supply nutrition during and after illness, in feverish and wasting disease, in loss of appetite and in poor nutrition, and for a weak constitution.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle (30 mL) at a time, 1 to 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Preparations containing royal jelly may cause asthma and serious allergic symptoms. People with asthma or allergy must not take it.

People with diabetes must not take this medicine. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to caramel, if your blood pressure is high, if you are an older person, or if you have heart or kidney trouble or swelling. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If there is no improvement in symptoms even after a long period of use, consult a doctor or pharmacist. This medicine is for oral use only; do not use it for injection. It can turn the urine yellow and so affect laboratory test results.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with preparations containing potassium, preparations containing liquorice, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).

If the amount of urine falls, if the face, hands or feet swell, if the eyelids feel heavy, if the hands become stiff, if blood pressure rises, or if headache, weakness, cramps of the limbs or paralysis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Tonic use and physical tiredness, and nutritional support during and after illness, in feverish and wasting disease, poor appetite and poor nutrition

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Eye drops (B16500COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for tired eyes, redness of the conjunctiva, discomfort of the eye after swimming or when dust or sweat has got into the eye, inflammation of the eye caused by ultraviolet and other light, soreness of the eyelids, discomfort when hard contact lenses are worn, itching of the eye, and blurring of the eye (for example when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 2 to 3 drops into the eye at a time, 5 to 6 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Infants aged 30 months and under must not use this medicine.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have severe pain in the eye, if you have had an allergy (redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash, reddening), if you have glaucoma, or if the user is a child.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Do not use it while soft contact lenses are being worn.
Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
Do not use the solution if it has become cloudy.
To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with other people as far as possible.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling occurs, or if blurring of the eye does not improve, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Tired eyes, conjunctival redness, eye inflammation from light, sore eyelids, itching and blurring, and eye discomfort after swimming or from dust

groups.title: Tablet (A82400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a nasal cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Those aged 8 to 14 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take it 3 times in 1 day, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are already taking another oral medicine containing phenylpropanolamine hydrochloride (a cold medicine, a medicine for rhinitis, a cough and expectorant medicine and the like), or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, high blood pressure, heart disorder, kidney disorder, oedema, glaucoma (for example eye pain, blurred vision), difficulty passing urine, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, a long-standing illness or a high fever; if you are pregnant or may become pregnant; if the user is an infant, a young child or an older person; or if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other oral medicines containing phenylpropanolamine hydrochloride (cold medicines, medicines for rhinitis, cough and expectorant medicines), other oral medicines for rhinitis, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold medicines, cough and expectorant medicines, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with preparations containing potassium, preparations containing liquorice, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).

If the amount of urine falls, if the face, hands or feet swell, if the eyelids feel heavy, if the hands become stiff, if blood pressure rises, or if headache or muscle disease (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Haemorrhagic stroke, nausea, vomiting, thirst, constipation, loss of appetite, rash, reddening and difficulty passing urine may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (A46800ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruising pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and to bring down fever when there are chills and a raised temperature.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet at a time, up to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak, have a high fever or are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of body fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or are unable to take fluid in; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Food Yellow No. 5.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol or diuretics.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding from the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, dizziness, hearing loss, oedema or tinnitus occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling, tightness of the chest, pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, generalised weakness or jaundice, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Headache, toothache and pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint, nerve, back and muscle pain, stiff shoulders, injury pain and period pain, and fever

groups.title: Capsule (132502ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for mild to moderate osteoarthritis (degenerative arthritis).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 capsules (400 to 800 mg) at a time, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have acute joint pain, if the user is under 16 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it.

If nausea or vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, erythema (red patches), hives, eczema, rash, a maculopapular rash, itching, oedema (swelling) or fluid retention occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Paste (D59900CPA)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of gingivitis (inflammation of the gums) and pyorrhoea of the tooth sockets — reddening, swelling and pus of the gums, and bad breath.
groups.usage: Put an appropriate amount for 1 application — about 0.3 g (about 0.5 cm) — on a toothbrush and massage the gums with it 2 times in 1 day (morning and evening). After use the mouth may be rinsed lightly with water.
groups.caution:
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have had an allergy to a medicine. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Use it in the mouth only.

If rash or reddening or itching occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (185430ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for allergic rhinitis (sneezing, blocked nose, itching, a burning feeling in the eyes) and for chronic idiopathic urticaria (hives of unknown cause).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 10 mL, 1 time in 1 day. Children aged 2 years and over but under 12 years: if the body weight is 30 kg or more, take 10 mL, 1 time in 1 day; if the body weight is 30 kg or less, take 5 mL, 1 time in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disorder or kidney failure.

Do not take it together with cimetidine, erythromycin, ketoconazole, quinidine, fluconazole or fluoxetine.

If sedation, an anticholinergic effect, headache, fainting, drowsiness, thirst, gastrointestinal disturbance (nausea, gastritis), increased appetite, rapid heartbeat, tiredness, rash, hair loss, anaphylaxis including angioedema, liver dysfunction, supraventricular tachyarrhythmia, palpitations, dizziness or seizures occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (A18300ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to prevent and relieve the dizziness, vomiting and headache of travel sickness.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and over: take 1 sachet (6 mL) at a time. Those aged 13 years and over but under 15 years: take 2/3 sachet (4 mL) at a time. The number of doses in 1 day is limited to 3. To prevent travel sickness, take it 30 minutes before boarding the vehicle or boat. If a further dose is needed, leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is broken down in the body to phenylalanine, so people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine must not take it.

Infants and young children under 3 years of age, and children aged 12 years and under, must not take this medicine. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have had symptoms of hypersensitivity to this medicine (rash, reddening, itching and the like); if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you have a respiratory disease such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis; or if you are an older person. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other anti-sickness medicines, cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives or cough and expectorant medicines. Avoid alcoholic drinks while you are taking it.

If rash, reddening, itching or thirst occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D99400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it; if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure, or severe acute or chronic kidney disease or kidney failure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain, blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, preparations containing potassium, preparations containing liquorice, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide) or flucloxacillin.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia or high anion gap metabolic acidosis occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters), asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), a fall in the amount of urine with swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache, muscle disease (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis), or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (a sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (A39600CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the symptoms of varicose veins (pain, a heavy feeling, swelling of the legs, cramp in the calf muscles), for blunt injury from an accident or from sport (haematoma, bruising, contusion, strain, sprain, swelling, pain of muscles and ligaments), and for superficial phlebitis, thrombophlebitis and treatment after sclerotherapy.
groups.usage: Use about 5 cm of the cream, apply it to the affected area and to the skin around it 2 to 3 times every day, and rub in gently. When applying it to the leg, massage lightly from below upwards. For phlebitis, do not rub it in; spread it thinly and then cover it with an occlusive dressing. This medicine has a strong cooling effect, so it is suitable for sensitive areas and for large areas.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to heparin, if you have a tendency to bleed or a low platelet count, or if you have thrombosis or thromboembolism; and do not use it on open wounds, on mucous membranes or on areas with a pus-forming infection. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding. Avoid contact with the conjunctiva of the eye.

If an allergy rarely occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Ointment (339200COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to prevent infection in minor cuts, grazes and burns.
groups.usage: After cleaning the wound, apply an appropriate amount to the wound 1 to 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or a perforated eardrum, and do not use it around the eyes. Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have a severe wound, a severe burn, a puncture wound, an animal bite or an ulcer of the skin. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine is for external use only; it must not be swallowed.

If rash, itching, reddening, swelling, papules, small blisters, a feeling of irritation or a superimposed infection occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with lithium or thiazide diuretics.

If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, swelling of the blood vessels, hives, an asthma attack, or swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and shortness of breath), a fall in platelets, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia (destruction of red cells), methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, rash, an allergic reaction, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms such as high fever, rash, reddening and burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth and eyes), generalised weakness, jaundice, cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, or high anion gap metabolic acidosis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Ointment (243302COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of chronic desquamative gingivitis and of intractable stomatitis and glossitis accompanied by erosion or ulceration.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to several times in 1 day. The amount may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it; if you have a tuberculous, viral or other pus-forming infection of the mouth; or if you have syphilis, chickenpox, a fungal infection, a bacterial skin infection, dermatitis around the mouth, rosacea, or gingivitis due to lack of vitamin C.
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, if the user is an infant or a child, or if the user is an older person.
Do not eat food immediately after use.
Do not use this medicine for the eyes.

If an infection of the mouth (a fungal or bacterial infection of the mouth) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
A feeling of numbness in the mouth, an abnormal or reduced sense of taste and, rarely, an allergic reaction may occur.

groups.title: Suspension (D53000ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to improve the symptoms of acid reflux, heartburn and indigestion caused by reflux of the stomach contents (for example after meals, during pregnancy, or together with reflux oesophagitis).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 10 to 20 mL at a time, 4 times in 1 day (after meals and before bedtime).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have congestive heart failure, kidney disorder, a high calcium level in the blood, nephrocalcinosis or recurrent calcium-containing kidney stones, or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with tetracycline, digoxin, fluoroquinolones, iron salts, ketoconazole, neuroleptics, thyroxine, penicillamine, beta blockers (atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), glucocorticoids, chloroquine, estramustine or diphosphonates. When it is taken with other medicines, leave an interval of 2 hours between them.

If an allergic reaction such as itching, narrowing of the airways or an anaphylactic reaction occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (123843ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum (phlegm) in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, bronchiectasis and pharyngitis, for the drainage of pus in chronic sinusitis, and for the drainage of fluid in secretory otitis media (of the middle ear).
groups.usage: Adults: at the start take 750 mg at a time, 3 times in 1 day; when symptoms improve, take 500 mg at a time, 3 times in 1 day. Those aged 13 years and over but 18 years and under: take 250 to 500 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Those aged 6 years and over but 12 years and under: take 250 mg at a time, 3 times in 1 day. Those aged 2 years and over but 5 years and under: take 250 to 500 mg in 1 day, divided into 4 doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, gastric or duodenal ulcer, or if the user is a child under 2 years of age. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disorder or heart disorder, if you have had gastric or duodenal ulcer, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, if you are an older person, or if you have hypersensitivity to caramel or have had it.

Do not mix it with syrups containing antibiotics or trimetoquinol hydrochloride; take them separately.

If nausea, vomiting, a feeling of abdominal bloating, gastrointestinal bleeding, heartburn or headache rarely occurs, or rhinitis in sensitive people, or from time to time loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, thirst, rash, erythema (red patches), eczema, itching, palpitations, runny nose or a feeling of pressure over the whole body, or Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), shock, anaphylaxis, a cough lasting 14 days or more, liver dysfunction with a rise in AST, ALT, ALP and LDH, or jaundice, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A35000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of nasal congestion (blocked nose), runny nose, headache and fever associated with a cold and with acute and subacute sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 tablet every 6 hours. Do not take more than 3 tablets in 24 hours. A separate instruction applies to people with severe kidney disorder (defined by creatinine clearance); that figure is cut off in the official text held for this product, so ask the pharmacist in the store.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to sympathomimetic amines; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks; if you have severe liver disorder or kidney disorder, severe high blood pressure or coronary artery disease, difficulty passing urine with residual urine, an overactive thyroid, diabetes or closed-angle glaucoma; if you have had a stroke or seizures; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if the user is a child under 15 years of age.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have difficulty passing urine because of an enlarged prostate, high blood pressure or coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, heart disease or an irregular heartbeat, asthma or a fall in blood pressure on standing; if you are an older person sensitive to dizziness and sedation; or if you are an older person with chronic constipation.
Athletes should be careful, as it may give a positive result in doping tests.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
If symptoms do not improve within 5 days, or if a high fever lasts for 3 days or more, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not use it together with MAO inhibitors, sleeping medicines, sedatives, antipsychotic medicines, antihistamines that depress the central nervous system, nasal decongestants, appetite suppressants, sympathomimetic medicines such as amphetamine-like stimulants, medicines that block sympathetic activity including bretylium, bethanidine, guanethidine, debrisoquine, methyldopa and beta or alpha-adrenergic blockers, or flucloxacillin.
Avoid alcoholic drinks while you are taking it.

If palpitations, rapid heartbeat, an irregular heartbeat, pallor of the face, cardiovascular collapse with low blood pressure, sedation, drowsiness, migraine, headache, dizziness, anxiety, tension, sweating, weakness, insomnia, hallucination, seizures, reversible posterior encephalopathy, reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome, stimulation or depression of the central nervous system, constipation, nausea, vomiting, digestive disturbance, ischaemic colitis (acute abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like), a skin reaction, temporary stinging pain, a burning feeling, rash, a lichenoid skin eruption, difficulty passing urine, retention of urine, closed-angle glaucoma, agitation, disturbed behaviour, insomnia, high blood pressure, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin reaction (fever, erythema, many small pustules and the like), high anion gap metabolic acidosis, thirst or sweating occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E38700ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruising pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and to bring down fever when there are chills (feeling cold and shivering) and a raised temperature.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 to 2 capsules at a time, 1 to 3 times in 1 day, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours. Those aged 8 years and over but under 15 years: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 to 3 times in 1 day, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours. Take it avoiding an empty stomach.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood fats, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have ever had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, or if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child aged 3 months and over but under 2 years; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergy to a medicine; if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of body fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea, are unable to take fluid in, or are taking a diuretic; or if you are taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Do not keep taking it over a long period.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
If symptoms do not improve after 5 or 6 doses, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving other medicines such as barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding from the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, dizziness or oedema occurs, or shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters), asthma, erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, a photosensitivity reaction (frequency unknown), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome, frequency unknown) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral liquid (391502ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for a feeling of heaviness in the legs, pain and restless legs caused by disorders of the venous and lymphatic circulation, and for the various symptoms related to haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 ampoule (7 mL) at a time, 1 time in 1 day. It is recommended that this medicine be taken with a glass of water during a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are in the first 3 months of pregnancy, if you are breast-feeding, if you have liver disease, if you are dependent on alcohol, if you have epilepsy, or if the user is a child.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine (rash, reddening, itching and the like) or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
This medicine is for oral use only; do not use it for injection.

If mild gastrointestinal disturbance, headache, facial flushing, rash, reddening, loss of appetite, nausea or vomiting occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E71100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruising pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and to bring down fever when there are chills and a raised temperature.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it; if you have had asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching; or if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure, or if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem.
If symptoms do not improve after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Do not keep taking it over a long period.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives while you are taking this medicine.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are receiving barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash and reddening, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation or oedema occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) — with hives, swelling and tightness of the chest appearing immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing — or Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, or liver dysfunction with generalised weakness and jaundice may occur; if so, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
